summary: Puzzling Lunar Mission Base is an interactive web application designed to simulate and solve complex logistical, structural, and resource-management challenges faced when establishing a sustainable human habitat on the Moon. Built using modern web technologies, the platform translates real lunar mission constraints—such as radiation shielding, power generation, life support systems, and terrain navigation—into engaging, puzzle-based scenarios. By combining NASA's lunar exploration data with interactive problem-solving, our project helps students, researchers, and space enthusiasts understand the critical engineering decisions required for long-term lunar habitation. Ultimately, it bridges the gap between complex space mission planning and accessible educational gameplay, inspiring the next generation of space explorers.
details:
How It Works & Key Features: Puzzling Lunar Mission Base places users in the role of a lunar mission architect. Players must strategically plan, build, and optimize a lunar base by solving interactive engineering and resource-allocation puzzles. Each level introduces realistic lunar variables, including limited solar energy during lunar nights, micrometeorite protection, thermal regulation, and oxygen/water recycling.

Benefits & Intended Impact: Designing a lunar base involves intricate trade-offs that are often difficult to visualize. This application makes space systems engineering intuitive and accessible, fostering critical thinking and STEM engagement while demonstrating the real-world challenges of NASA's Artemis missions.

Tools & Technologies Used:

  • Platform & Frontend: Developed and hosted via Base44 web application framework ([https://puzzling-lunar-mission-base.base44.app](https://puzzling-lunar-mission-base.base44.app)).
  • Data & Research: Based on NASA lunar surface, environmental, and Artemis mission parameters.
  • Design & Logic: Interactive puzzle mechanics engineered to reflect real-world physics and resource constraints.

Creativity & Considerations: Rather than presenting static information, we gamified actual aerospace engineering constraints so users learn through trial, error, and strategic optimization.
